newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds ended higher on Wednesday but well off initial peaks as the peseta weakened versus the mark, dealers said.
Trading was listless, especially in cash securities. Bonos tracked foreign markets without any domestic incentive.
"The Italian market is really strong but Spain's debt market had already priced in all positive expectations for the country to be in the first EMU wave," a dealer in Madrid said.
Bonos underperformed BTPs. The 10-year spread between the two markets fell to around 19 basis points versus 22 on Tuesday.

The market was unchanged after data showing the central government public deficit rose to 1.7 percent of gross domestic product in the first half of 1997 versus 1.1 percent in the first five months through May.
Spain's central government deficit target for the overall year is 2.5 percent and the government said it will meet it.
